annotate_archive_key: Archive: out of the two zones, still in all mail and search (e)
annotate_is_archived: Archived: out of Conversations and Notifications, still in All mail, its labels and search.
area_downgraded_hint: Mail to unclaimed prefixes, or that failed DMARC. Hidden everywhere else.
area_leaks_hint: Claimed prefixes that got mail from senders they were not given to, or mail pretending to be one of those senders. Set whom a prefix was given to above its mail, or with {#code}yuuka prefix expect{/code}.
area_unclaimed_hint: Addresses that got mail without being claimed. Claim one here, or with {#code}yuuka prefix claim{/code}.
auth_enroll_done_link: The passkey is stored. The link is used up; sign in with the new passkey.
auth_enroll_done_session: The passkey is stored. It works from the next sign-in.
auth_enroll_link_once: This link registers one passkey and then expires. Registering does not sign you in.
auth_enroll_needs_link: This page needs a one-time enrollment link. Run {#code}yuuka admin enroll{/code} on the server, or use a recovery code at {#recover}/recover{/recover}.
auth_err_invalid_state: This authenticator already holds a passkey for yuuka.
auth_err_not_allowed: The passkey prompt was cancelled or timed out.
auth_err_security: This page's origin does not match the configured WebUI origin.
auth_err_too_many: Too many attempts. Wait a moment and try again.
auth_login_hint: Use a passkey registered for this mailbox.
auth_login_no_passkey: No passkey yet? Run {#code}yuuka admin enroll{/code} on the server for a one-time link.
auth_recover_bad_code: That code did not work. Check it and try again; each code works once.
auth_recover_hint: A recovery code lets you register one new passkey. It does not sign you in, works once, and the operator is alerted when it is used.
auth_unsupported: This browser does not support passkeys.
credentials_on_host: Tokens and SMTP passwords are issued on the host; here they can be seen and revoked.
credentials_revoke_cost: {who}'s next call with it fails; a new one is issued on the host.
credentials_revoke_cost_smtp: {who}'s next SMTP submission with it is refused; a new one is issued on the host.
drafter_accepted: Accepted, and the rule is saved. It runs on mail that arrives from now on.
drafter_no_candidates: This message has no sender, list or receiving prefix to draw a condition from.
drafter_not_past: Mail already here is left alone until you apply the rule to it.
drafter_saved: Rule saved. It runs on mail that arrives from now on.
drafter_title: Handle mail like this from now on
drafter_title_accept: Accept, and handle mail like this from now on
drafter_when: Mail like this is mail where
facts_auth_not_received: none: sent by this system, never received
grant_cost_allowlist: {who}'s mail as {as} to anyone not on the allowlist stays a draft.
grant_cost_allowlist_remove: {who}'s mail as {as} to the entries taken off stays a draft.
grant_cost_draft: Every submission by {who} as {as} stays a draft until a person confirms it.
grant_cost_hold: Mail the review passes waits {window} for a recall before it is sent.
grant_cost_limit: {who}'s submissions as {as} beyond the new limit stay drafts.
grant_cost_none: {who} may no longer use {as}: SMTP submissions are refused, the rest stay drafts.
grant_cost_review: {who}'s mail as {as} goes through the review checks and waits out a recall window before it is sent.
grant_cost_suspend: Every submission by {who} as {as} stays a draft, and its held mail is recalled instead of sent, until resumed on the host.
grant_cost_thread: {who}'s mail as {as} to anyone outside the thread it answers stays a draft.
grants_none: No grants. Without one, the defaults of each kind of principal apply.
grants_nothing_tighter: Nothing is tighter than this grant short of removing it.
grants_on_host: Grants are added and raised on the host; here they can be seen, tightened and removed.
grants_opt_new: New recipients per day at most
grants_owner_capped: Capped at drafts: the address belongs to {owner}, and only they send as it. Stored: {stored}.
grants_remove_widens: Removing it lets more through: the default is wider in {fields}. Only on the host:
grants_suspended_why: Suspended: every submission stays a draft. Resuming lets mail through again, so it is done on the host:
grants_tighten_legend: One change at a time, only tighter than now
grants_widening: That lets more through; the WebUI only tightens. On the host:
history_archived: Archived, so it is in neither zone. The changes:
history_classifier: In {zone}, as yuuka's classifier put it. The changes:
history_empty: Nobody has labelled, moved or archived it.
history_label: Where its labels, zone and archived state came from
history_moved: In {zone}, moved there by {who}. The changes:
identities_disable_cost: Nothing more goes out as {address}: submissions stay drafts, held mail is recalled instead of sent.
identities_on_host: Identities are added on the host; here they can be seen and disabled.
identities_taken_over: Disabling it would hand the address to {pattern}, its owner and its grants, which may let more through. Only on the host:
label_case_differs: Labels are case-sensitive; in use already:
label_reserved: Cannot start with $ or a backslash
leak_given_to_nobody: given to nobody yet: {#code}yuuka prefix expect{/code}
leak_none: No claimed prefix got mail it should not have.
nav_leaks_title: claimed prefixes that got mail from senders they were not given to
nav_outbox_unknown: may have been sent: waiting for a decision
nav_proposals_title: suggested by agents, waiting for your decision
notes_cites_label: Cites: the passages the note relies on
notes_delete_cost: Removes {who}'s note; the mail itself does not change.
notes_delete_cost_own: Removes your note; the mail itself does not change.
notes_needs_cite: A note cites at least one passage.
notes_no_selection: Select text in the mail first.
notes_placeholder: What this mail is about, for you and whoever reads it later. Plain text.
offer_moved_conversations: Moved to Conversations. Do the same for mail like this from now on?
offer_moved_notifications: Moved to Notifications. Do the same for mail like this from now on?
prefix_expect_hint: Domains, separated by commas; empty clears them.
prefix_unclaim_cost: Its mail is downgraded again and leaves the zones; nothing is deleted.
prefix_unclaimed_facts: Not claimed: its mail is downgraded and nothing about it notifies.
problem_widening: That lets more through; the WebUI only tightens.
proposal_conflict: This proposal was decided already, or has expired
proposal_expired: Expired: nobody decided it in time. Nothing was changed.
read_link_mismatch: The text names another site; this link goes to {host}
read_no_anchor: There is no {anchor} in this message; it may have been cited from an older view.
reading_fold_facts: Fold the facts into one line
review_advisory: Worth a look before it goes; these hold nothing back:
review_found_code: a code in the {where}, extracted from
review_found_link: a sign-in link in the {where}, extracted from
review_link_unseen: — {domain} never seen from a verified sender, a recipient or the allowlist
review_recall_conflict: It is no longer held: already released, or already recalled.
review_recall_cost: Nothing is sent; it goes back to Drafts. Two recalls by a person within a day suspend the grant.
review_recall_not_yours: Only a person, or whoever submitted it, can recall it ({scope}).
review_recalled: Recalled: back in Drafts, nothing was sent.
review_ref_unknown: is no message the sender can see
review_resume_on_host: Every submission stays a draft until it is resumed on the host:
review_suspended: Recalled twice within a day: {who}'s grant on {identity} is suspended.
review_suspended_others: Its other held mail ({n}) was recalled too.
review_unreadable: cannot be read by the checks
rule_apply_disabled: Only an enabled rule that this version understands can be applied
rule_json_invalid: Not a match tree: one of all, any, not, or field/op/value.
rule_json_only: These conditions do not fit the form; edit them as JSON.
rule_preview_failed: {failed} ran out of time and do not match
rule_preview_needs_action: Choose what it does to see how much mail it would change.
rule_preview_overruled: {overruled} keep what a person or an agent decided
rule_priority_hint: Rules run lowest first; the first match sets the zone, archive and notification, labels add up
rule_revert_cost: Every change this rule made to mail is set back, unless someone changed it again since. The rule itself stays.
rule_warn_unverified_from: Anyone can forge From: add “From proven by DMARC is yes”
rules_arrival_only: A rule runs on mail as it arrives. Changing it does not change mail already here; apply or take back does.
rules_delete_cost: It stops running; what it did stays until taken back.
rules_hint: Rules run on mail as it arrives, in order. They only label, move, archive and quiet notifications; nothing a rule does sends mail.
rules_none: No rules yet. “Mail like this…” in the reading pane drafts one from a message.
rules_unsupported_why: This version cannot evaluate the rule, so it matches nothing:
send_body_placeholder: Write in Markdown. > quotes, a blank line starts a paragraph.
send_confirm_detail: it is queued with you as the approver (§8.9)
send_held_no_grant: Held as a draft: no grant
send_held_nothing_sent: Nothing was sent. The draft stays in Drafts; a person can confirm it there.
send_held_nothing_sent_owner: Nothing was sent. The draft stays in Drafts; only {name} can confirm it.
send_no_draft_scope: This session may not write drafts ({scope}).
send_no_grant_theirs: the address is {owner}'s, and you have no grant to send as it
send_no_grant_yours: the address is yours, and you have no grant to send as it
send_no_identities: No identity to send as. Add one with {#code}yuuka identity add{/code} and {#code}yuuka grant set{/code}.
send_no_identity_detail: the draft is kept, but it cannot be sent as it is
send_only_owner_confirms: Held: only {name} can confirm mail as this address
send_only_owner_sends: Held: only {name} can send as this address
send_only_owner_sends_detail: it is {name}'s, and you cannot send as it (§8.9)
send_problem_conflict: Already submitted: the draft has gone to the outbox
send_problem_invalid_body: Something in the draft is not valid
send_problem_no_identity: No identity covers this From address
send_problem_not_found: Not found: it may have been deleted
send_problem_rate_limited: Too many requests; try again in a moment
send_problem_scope_required: This session is not allowed to do that
send_problem_unauthenticated: The session has ended; sign in again
send_problem_unavailable: yuuka is busy; try again in a moment
send_resolve_abandon_risk: Records it as not sent. Nothing more is sent; if the first attempt did arrive, it stays arrived.
send_resolve_resend_risk: Queues it again for the unknown recipients. If the first attempt did arrive, they get the message twice.
send_resolve_sent_risk: Records the unknown recipients as having received it. Choose this when you know it arrived: a reply, or the exit's own log.
send_smtp_note: Submitted over SMTP: the message is kept as the client sent it and is not edited here. Send it as it is, or delete it.
send_tier_review_now: review — sent right after the checks
send_unknown_body: The exit was handed the whole message, then the answer was lost. It may have been delivered or not; yuuka cannot tell, so it does not retry on its own.
send_unknown_only_person: Only a person signed in with {scope} can decide this.
shell_keys: {#k}j{/k} {#k}k{/k} move · {#k}/{/k} search · {#k}r{/k} reply · {#k}c{/k} compose · {#k}e{/k} archive · {#k}l{/k} label · {#k}Esc{/k} close
shell_pick_outbox_row: Pick a row to see each recipient and the attempts.
shell_pick_prefix: Pick a prefix to list its mail.
shell_pick_proposal: Pick a proposal to open the mail it is about.
undo_superseded: {n} changed again since, left as they are
x_code_title: Code found by yuuka in the {source} (confidence {confidence})
x_unverified_title: No DMARC pass from the trusted receiver: the sender is unproven
